topics.topic: Validation path and malformed-parameter handling for MCP discovery methods under State 4
questions: Do `initialize`, `ping` and `tools/list` bypass the operation-schema and actor checks after size, token and depth, or must they also pass those checks under State 4's common boundary?
Are MCP discovery methods exempt from the known-operation and operation-schema checks, and if so, who validates their protocol parameters and what happens when those parameters are malformed?
After size, token and depth pass, must `initialize`, `ping` and `tools/list` also pass method-specific schema validation, and what happens on an unknown or malformed field?

quotes: answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; the depth check of the request message below, else invalid_request; for tools/call, the message names a catalogue operation, fits that operation's request model as fit_request decides, called with that request model and the canonical_bytes of the arguments' JSON text, holds every bound below, measured on the fitted request before any JSON text in it is replaced, and has every JSON text it carries then made canonical by the replacement below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else raise NotPermittedError; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1). initialize, ping and tools/list name no catalogue operation and are answered after the depth check, as the note on methods says.

answer_request: [BEHAVIOR] The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, parsed only after the depth check, which follows the size and token checks. A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing. A request's method decides: initialize answers the result {protocolVersion: the imported MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: the imported MCP_SERVER_NAME constant, version: the imported MCP_SERVER_VERSION constant}} whatever version its params ask, and keeps no state; ping answers an empty result object; tools/list answers {tools: [...]} as below, ignoring any cursor; tools/call names the catalogue operation in params.name and carries its request in params.arguments, which then pass the remaining checks of the first note.
judgement.why: The later notes explicitly exempt discovery methods from catalogue-operation schema and actor checks and define their protocol-level handling after size, token, and depth validation.

topics.topic: Definition, creation, and sandbox exposure of own_proc
questions: What concrete resource is `own_proc`, who creates it, and is it an additional mounted or otherwise exposed sandbox resource despite the prose saying the environment holds only the previously listed resources?

quotes: execute_function: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST start bubblewrap with new user, PID, IPC, UTS and network namespaces and no network interface but the new namespace's own loopback, which bubblewrap brings up, with no capability option, the environment cleared and then set exactly to the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant, exactly the host paths of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant bound read-only, inside the new root the symbolic links of the imported SANDBOX_ROOT_SYMLINKS constant (each name linking to its target, made by bubblewrap --symlink), one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write, bubblewrap's own fresh proc mounted at the imported SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT constant and minimal dev mounts, and no other host directory; the child dies with its parent, and the runner is the init of the new PID namespace (bubblewrap --as-pid-1), so bubblewrap exits only after the host kernel has killed and reaped every other process of that namespace. The interpreter it starts there is os.path.realpath(sys.executable), the kernel's own CPython under a path of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant, never a launcher such as a virtual environment's.

runner_arguments: [BEHAVIOR] MUST return exactly two arguments: the decimal number launch.channel_fd, the descriptor the program writes every message to, which is the parent's own pipe end inherited at that number; and one JSON text with the members exchange_directory, code_file, inputs (each port, carriage, cardinality and files), output_ports (each name, carriage and cardinality), and memory_bytes, process_count and output_bytes of launch.bounds; its member file_size_limit is the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant; its member environment is the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant; its member readable_paths is the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant; its member raise_on_call is the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_FUNCTIONS constant; its member raise_without_argument is the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT constant; its member raise_on_every_method is the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_CLASS constant; its member raise_unseeded is the imported SANDBOX_UNSEEDED_CONSTRUCTOR constant; its member proc_directory is the imported SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT constant; the program reads exactly these two arguments after its own path.
judgement.why: The later notes define `own_proc` as bubblewrap's fresh proc mount, assign its creation to `execute_function`, and pass its mount location to the runner as `proc_directory`.
